## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

AndroidManifest.xml — app-wear/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml

## Trigger

The sensor permission request run by SensorPermissionManager.onLaunch
and SensorPermissionManager.requestAgain, through
SensorPermissionSystemImpl.requestPermission — observed, but it only
ever requests the single permission held in SENSOR_PERMISSION
(BODY_SENSORS or health.READ_HEART_RATE), never
ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION.

## Today

app-wear/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml declares VIBRATE,
BLUETOOTH_CONNECT, BODY_SENSORS (maxSdkVersion 35) and
health.READ_HEART_RATE; android.permission.ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION
appears nowhere in the manifest, the Kotlin sources or the resource
files. SensorPermissionSystemImpl's SENSOR_PERMISSION constant and its
isGranted/canShowSystemPrompt/requestPermission trio are built around
one permission string only — the one sensorPermissionFor(sdkInt)
returns — and ActivityResultLauncher<String> in SensorPermissionManager's
call chain launches that single string. Without the manifest entry,
Health Services' ExerciseClient refuses startExerciseAsync() with a
SecurityException naming ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION, and strips the data
types depending on it (lap distance, workout speed, and others) before
the exercise session is ever reached.

## Expected

app-wear/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml declares
android.permission.ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION as a `<uses-permission>`, and
the app requests it at runtime through the same permission parcours
already used for the sensor permission — SensorPermissionManager,
SensorPermissionScreen, SensorPermissionSystemImpl — rather than
through a second, parallel path. Because that parcours' request
mechanism (SensorPermissionSystemImpl.requestPermission,
ActivityResultLauncher<String>, SENSOR_PERMISSION) is built to launch
exactly one permission string at a time, requesting two dangerous
permissions (the existing sensor one and ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION) through
it is a second gap: the launcher/request signature has to accept more
than one permission — for instance
ActivityResultContracts.RequestMultiplePermissions(), or an added
second request step — and isGranted/canShowSystemPrompt have to report
on both permissions, not just SENSOR_PERMISSION, for the exercise
session to actually reach ExerciseClient.
